# memo's one-page design: what memo is and why. spec.md says it at length.

title memo, on one sheet

actor you    amber   the developer
actor agent  cyan    an agent, each job in a fresh context
actor memo   green   the tool and its store
actor repo   violet  git

line arrow work moves
line dotted @memo reads or writes the store
mark balloon part
mark flag asked of a project
mark diamond @you your attention
mark more more

::: titleblock
cell id | 1 · Premise · sheet 1 of 1
wordmark mem@memo{o}
motto The memory and the process of a project built with agents
para A command-line tool and a local web page over one store per repository; a skill or brief for each role an agent plays; and drains that work the queue unattended, each task in its own checkout.

cell problem | Problem — without memo
lead Agents forget everything between sessions, and do what is cheapest rather than what they are told:
point P1 | A fresh session rediscovers the code and guesses at past decisions. | {1}
point P2 | The developer is asked how code should work, and not what the product should do. | {9}
point P3 | An agent takes the cheapest path to whatever "done" is checked: it narrows the task and dismisses what review finds. | {4} {7}
point P4 | Telling an agent how to behave changes nothing; a required output or a failing check does. | {11}
point P5 | An agent copies the nearest code, so copies of a rule drift apart. | {10} ▲2
point P6 | Several agents working at once trip over each other. | {5} ▲4

cell answer | Solution — with memo
big The @repo{repository} keeps what is true now; @memo{memo} keeps what happened and why.
para **Done is an acceptance test, written in planning before the implementer starts.** Fresh agents review and check, and the implementer fixes every confirmed defect and dismisses none.
para **Human attention is the scarcest resource.** A project is healthy when only product questions reach the developer and escaped defects trend down.

cell attn | Your attention goes here, and only here
item ◆1 | **Planning** with the tech lead: you judge what each task will do, never its code.
item ◆2 | **Product questions**, batched in the inbox, answered in a word.
item ◆3 | **A retrospective**: patterns across runs, as a handful of decisions.
item ◆4 | **Curation**: confirming where each recurring lesson goes.
item ◆5 | **A defect you notice**: traced to the task, run and step that let it through.
:::

view 2 WORKFLOW | one task, from a note to landed code | a lane for each actor · time runs left to right

::: swimlane
lane @you
lane @agent | fresh agents, | one job each
lane @memo | the tool and | its store
lane @repo

phase 1 | NOTE AND PLAN
phase 2 | DRAIN
phase 3 | RUN: A FRESH AGENT FOR EACH JOB
phase 4 | LAND
phase 5 | LOOK BACK

# 1 note and plan
box note @you 1.1 | **write a note** | any time
box plan @you 1.2 | **plan it** ◆1 | judge contracts
box lead @agent 1.2 | **TECH LEAD** | scope and order, | the how decided
more The tech lead does its own discovery, decides the order and scope of the tasks, and brings the how already decided. It asks you only what the software should do, and applies a principle you have stated before rather than asking again.
box tasks @memo 1.1-2 | TASKS ▲3 | story · bug · refactor | acceptance tests | written here
more A story carries its contract and its acceptance test. A bug carries its reproduction, run in planning, and its class with the search behind it. A refactor names a rule, its home to be and its copies, in domain words. memo refuses a task that lacks what its kind requires.
arrow note lead
arrow lead plan
arrow plan lead
arrow lead tasks

# 2 drain
box drainit @you 2 chip | **drain a label**
box queue @memo 2 | QUEUE | by priority, | dependencies first | ◂ surveys' tasks, from 5
box worktree @repo 2 | **own checkout** ▲4 | on its own branch
arrow tasks queue
arrow drainit queue
arrow queue worktree

# 3 run
box ask @you 3.2-4 | **answer product questions** ◆2 | nothing else reaches you
box mend @agent 3.1 note | rebaser: | test setup
box impl @agent 3.2 | IMPLEMENT | plan names | each rule's home
more Before any code, the implementer lists each rule the change computes and where it is computed today, and builds on that home. It works until the acceptance test and the check command pass. It may widen the task, with a reason; it may not narrow it, or touch the acceptance test.
box review @agent 3.3 | REVIEW ▲2 | findings and | their siblings, | each a failing test
more A fresh reviewer, given the task and the diff and nothing of the implementer's reasoning, backs each finding with a failing test, and searches the code the change reads for other instances of its class. There are two rounds.
box check @agent 3.4 | CHECK | real or not; | binds the run
more A fresh checker runs each finding's evidence and judges only whether the defect is real, never whether it is worth fixing. A confirmed finding binds the run: the implementer fixes it and cannot dismiss it. Last, the checker confirms each fix by the reviewer's own test.
box accept @memo 3.1 | ACCEPTANCE | its test fails | on main
more memo runs the task's acceptance test against main: a story's behaviour must be missing, and a bug must reproduce. If main moved and only the setup broke, the rebaser repairs the setup and may not change an assertion. A bug whose test passes on main asks you "already fixed?".
arrow worktree accept
arrow accept impl
arrow impl review
arrow review check
arrow impl ask
arrow ask impl
detail A | accept impl review check

# 4 land
box rebaser @agent 4 note | rebaser: | on a conflict
box land @memo 4 | LAND ▲1 | rebase, checks, | test unchanged, | fixes held | @memo{**memo decides**}
box main @repo 4 | **main** | fast-forwarded
arrow check land
arrow land main

# 5 look back
box look @you 5.1-2 | ◆3 **retrospective** | ◆4 **curation** | ◆5 **a defect:** trace
box surveys @agent 5.3 | SURVEYS | debt: a rule | and its copies | mutation: a | verdict per mutant
box measures @memo 5.1 | MEASURES | product questions | escapes per 1k lines | cost and context
box lessons @repo 5.2-3 | **check, standard,** | **glossary** ▲5 | from a pattern | that recurs
arrow land measures
arrow measures surveys
arrow measures look
arrow look lessons
:::

::: details
detail A | Detail A — where a run's stop goes | **The inbox holds product questions only**; every other stop has an owner.
rung @memo | 1 · Retry | memo | A usage limit or a logged-out tool is retried, and a drain stops on a failure every task would share.
rung @agent | 2 · Resolve | an agent | A conflict, or a test's setup broken by main moving, goes to the rebaser. A broken tool becomes a task the run waits on.
rung @you | 3 · Ask | you answer | What the software should do, look like or cover, with options, a lean, and before-and-after output or images. The answer requeues the task, and a principle in it joins the standard.

notes | General notes — what memo asks of a project
note 1 | A check command runs every check, and a black-box suite drives the built product from outside. | Landing runs it.
note 2 | A glossary of domain words and a standard of principles, both checked in. | The tech lead, reviewer and debt survey use them.
note 3 | Prototypes checked in, where every run can see them. | A page's look.
note 4 | No fixed ports and no state outside a checkout, so runs can go in parallel. | Drains run side by side.
note 5 | Guidance that runs may edit; a check refuses any widened permission. | Drains improve guidance too.
foot On the drawings, each flag marks where its note applies; hover either to find the other.
:::

view 3 SYSTEM | the key pieces, and why each exists | balloons key the drawing to the parts list · hover either to find the other

::: assembly
person dev @you A1-A7 | DEVELOPER | you
box notes @memo B1 | NOTES {2} | an idea, any time | **plan it** opens | a session
box lead @agent B2 | TECH LEAD {3} | a skill in your session | tasks and their tests
box drain @memo B3-B4 | DRAIN {5} | a label's tasks | by priority, honouring | dependencies, within | a budget; drains run | side by side ▲4
box inbox @memo B5 | INBOX {9} | product questions only
box retro @agent B6 | RETRO · CURATION {11} | patterns → decisions
box viewer @memo B7 | VIEWER {12} | patterns before items

group run C1-C4 | A RUN · ONE JOB PER FRESH AGENT {6}
box rebaser @agent C1 | REBASER | brings a run up to | date with main
box impl @agent C2 | IMPLEMENTER | the change, built on | each rule's home
box reviewer @agent C3 | REVIEWER {7} | findings and siblings, | each a failing test
box checker @agent C4 | CHECKER | real or not; | whether a fix holds
store store @memo C5-C6 | MEMO STORE {1} | one file per repository | [NOTES] [TASKS {4}] [RUNS] | [FINDINGS] [ESCAPES]
box surveys @agent C7 | SURVEYS {10} | debt survey, | mutation survey

valve land @memo | {8} ▲1
group repo @repo D1-E4 | THE REPO · WHAT IS TRUE NOW
rail main @repo D1-D4 | MAIN
box truth @repo E1-E4 | WHAT IS TRUE NOW | @repo{■} code and tests | @repo{■} prototypes ▲3 | @repo{■} glossary, standard {13} | @repo{■} guidance ▲5

arrow dev notes
arrow dev lead
arrow dev drain
arrow dev inbox
arrow dev retro
arrow dev viewer
arrow notes lead
arrow drain run
arrow run main via land
arrow main truth
arrow run store dotted @memo | found from every checkout
arrow inbox store dotted
arrow surveys store dotted @memo | tasks from evidence
arrow store viewer dotted
arrow store truth @agent | a pattern that recurs | → a check, the standard

parts PARTS LIST | what memo is made of, and why each part exists
part 1 @memo | The store | notes, tasks, runs, questions, findings, escapes; one file per repository | What happened and why outlives every session, and the store arbitrates every run writing at once.
part 2 @memo | Notes | an idea not yet work, with a button to plan it | An idea reaches agents without the developer opening a session first.
part 3 @agent | Tech lead | a skill: discovery, scope, order, tasks | Scope and contract are set before any code by an agent with no diff to keep small, while the developer judges only what.
part 4 @memo | Tasks | a story, bug or refactor, each with its own proof | Done is an acceptance test written before the implementer starts, so the implementer cannot narrow the task.
part 5 @memo | Drains | a label's tasks by priority, unattended | Work gets done while the developer is elsewhere, within a budget.
part 6 @agent | A run | rebaser, implementer, reviewer and checker, each fresh | One job per context limits bias and spreads the context.
part 7 @agent | Review | findings and siblings, each a failing test a checker runs | The author is the weakest judge of its own work, so a confirmed finding binds it.
part 8 @memo | Landing | rebase, the check command, the acceptance test unchanged, the fixes held | memo, not the agent, decides whether work lands.
part 9 @you | Inbox | product questions only, batched | The developer's attention goes only where only they can decide.
part 10 @agent | Surveys | the debt survey and the mutation survey | Agents copy the nearest code, so the codebase's health is budgeted for.
part 11 @agent | Retrospective and curation | patterns as decisions; a category of escape seen twice gets a check | The process improves from evidence rather than from words.
part 12 @memo | Viewer | a local page: the inbox, drains, health, notes, landed pages | The project's state at a glance, patterns before items.
part 13 @repo | Glossary and standard | domain words; the principles review judges by | Rules have names, and the developer's answers become the bar.
:::
